title: SableBridge - Security & Hosting Options Discovery
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment
summary: Initial security posture discovery with SableBridge CISO and infra. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for inference. Primary concerns: KMS and BYOK, audit logs retention, SSO/SAML + SCIM, SOC2 evidence and pen test history, RBAC scoping, and EU data residency. Agreed next steps: share SOC2 report, private deployment checklist, and proposed PoC plan for a limited private deployment and baseline perf numbers.
action_items: Jordan Reed: Share SOC 2 Type II report and recent penetration test summary (due: 2028-06-18)
Maya Lin: Provide private deployment checklist and network diagram template (due: 2028-06-19)
Priya Shah: Send list of required compliance artifacts and preferred retention windows (due: 2028-06-20)
next_steps: Jordan to email SOC2 and pen test artifacts + compliance contact links
Schedule 1-hour technical deep dive with SableBridge infra (Maya + Mark) next week
Provision trial dedicated instance for performance baseline (if NDAs ok)
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2028-06-15 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 47 mins
Attendees: Jordan Reed (Redwood AE), Maya Lin (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (SableBridge CISO), Mark Delaney (Infra Lead), Elena Ortiz (Compliance Manager)

[00:00:00] Jordan Reed: hey everybody, thanks for carving out time today, um we're Jordan from Redwood, with Maya on the call as our solutions engineer. just to confirm, priya, mark, elena, is this still a good time?
[00:00:12] Priya Shah: yes thanks jordan, this is priya, i'm the ciso, and yep good to go.
[00:00:20] Mark Delaney: Mark here, infra lead, sound good.
[00:00:24] Elena Ortiz: Elena, compliance, yep we have about 45 minutes.
[00:00:30] Jordan Reed: perfect. quick agenda — security posture intake, our hosting options (hosted, dedicated reserved capacity, private vpc/onprem), keys and encryption model, audit logs & retention, and then next steps. anything to add?
[00:00:45] Priya Shah: want to focus on BYOK and how keys are managed, plus what audit trails look like. also retention and egress controls — we have european customer data so residency matters.
[00:00:55] Jordan Reed: understood. maya, quick intro?
[00:01:00] Maya Lin: sure hi everyone, i'm maya, i work on infra and private deployments. i'll jump in on the technical details around kms, key isolation, RBAC and the private control plane.
[00:01:12] Jordan Reed: great. so at a high level, redwood offers three modes: hosted api where we run the model and manage keys, dedicated reserved where you get predictable capacity and a customer-isolated tenant, and private which can be vpc-hosted or on-prem where control plane boundaries are adjusted.
[00:01:30] Priya Shah: quick question — for hosted, you say you manage keys. do you offer customer-managed keys in that mode or is that only for dedicated/private?
[00:01:40] Maya Lin: good question. for hosted, we do offer an encryption-at-rest model with our managed KMS by default. we also support BYOK via customer KMS integration for dedicated and private first-class. recently we've added a limited BYOK bridging for hosted with an enterprise add-on — it goes through a key-wrapping flow with your cloud KMS. it's a bit more constrained because we can't import keys into our HSMs on hosted shared infra.
[00:02:05] Mark Delaney: can you be more specific — by constrained do you mean we lose some features or there's a compliance gap?
[00:02:12] Maya Lin: constraint mainly around FIPS/HSM-backed operations. hosted BYOK path uses wrapped keys where the master key stays in your KMS and we receive wrapped data keys; we don't host the master in an HSM under your tenancy. so if your compliance requires FIPS 140-2 HSM under your control for every cryptographic op, you'll likely want dedicated with an option to colocate HSMs or private on-prem.
[00:02:36] Elena Ortiz: that aligns — our vendor policy requires HSM-backed key custody for some regulated products. is there an attestation or diagram you can share?
[00:02:45] Jordan Reed: absolutely. we'll share the architecture diagram and the BYOK flow doc — it shows where the key wrapping happens, KMS integrations for AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, and Azure KeyVault. we'll include note about limitations for hosted BYOK.
[00:02:56] Priya Shah: can you outline audit logs — what gets captured and for how long by default? retention controls?
[00:03:05] Maya Lin: by default we capture request metadata, model id, token counts, timestamps, requester id, and broad operational logs. we also capture a per-request trace for latency and error reasons. PII in payloads is not redacted automatically in logs unless you opt into payload redaction — we recommend that for regulated workloads. default retention is 90 days for hosted audit logs, with options to extend in enterprise retention add-on. for dedicated and private you can configure longer retention and ship logs to your SIEM via syslog or cloud logging sinks.
[00:03:34] Mark Delaney: shipping to our cloud logging is important — we need <company>-side retention policies and ability to purge. is purge API available?
[00:03:42] Maya Lin: yes for dedicated/private you get log export and purge controls. for hosted, purge requests are handled via support and subject to data service windows; we can push for faster windows with an enterprise contract.
[00:03:55] Priya Shah: data residency — we operate in EU and need guaranteed non-US access for EU data. do you have region locking?
[00:04:04] Jordan Reed: we do region routing policies. for hosted we can pin workloads to EU regions and restrict fallback, but strict legal guarantees for residency are stronger in dedicated and private where you can choose placement. we'll surface the routing policy config and SLA language.
[00:04:18] Elena Ortiz: what about RBAC and SSO — we use SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning. can you integrate with our identity provider?
[00:04:26] Maya Lin: yes, we support SSO via SAML and OIDC and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC supports roles at org, project, and token level, and you can bind groups from your IdP. we also have token scoping for service tokens (model-level, route-level), and audit trails for admin actions.
[00:04:43] Mark Delaney: do tokens expire and can we enforce rotation?
[00:04:47] Maya Lin: tokens can be short lived via OAuth flows or long lived for service tokens, we recommend rotating service tokens regularly and we support automatic rotation if you enable it in the dedicated/private control plane.
[00:04:58] Priya Shah: SOC2 and ISO — do you have both? and can we get the latest report?
[00:05:05] Jordan Reed: yes we are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified, and we'll share the latest attestation. note the reports require an NDA or an access request depending on the level of detail — we'll include next steps to request them.
[00:05:18] Elena Ortiz: do you do regular pen tests and vuln disclosure?
[00:05:22] Maya Lin: we have annual 3rd-party penetration tests and a public bug bounty program with triage. we can provide a summary of the last pentest and remediation windows.
[00:05:32] Priya Shah: for the private deployment, how isolated is the control plane? is telemetry still routed through redwood or can we host the whole control plane?
[00:05:42] Maya Lin: good nuance. private mode offers two patterns: private control plane (hosted in your VPC) where you keep metadata and keys in your tenancy and Redwood provides a management endpoint; and on-prem full stack where the control plane can be entirely customer-managed. in private vpc the telemetry can be routed to your sink, and we can disable outgoing telemetry if required for air-gapped setups.
[00:06:02] Mark Delaney: what about model artifacts — do you ever persist model weights or cache on shared disks?
[00:06:08] Maya Lin: model weights are read-only artifacts; on hosted they exist on our storage but not shared across tenants in a writable way. for dedicated/private you can provide your own model packages or pin versions. KV caches and runtime caches are tenant isolated.
[00:06:20] Priya Shah: retention policy for prompts and replies — we need to ensure retention windows are configurable and ability to opt out of storing prompts.
[00:06:29] Jordan Reed: we support configurable payload retention. hosted defaults to transient caching for 30 days unless you enable long-term logging; dedicated/private gives full control. there's also an opt-out flag — you can pass a sensitive=true header to avoid storing the payload. we'll include docs for that API.
[00:06:46] Elena Ortiz: do you have out-of-the-box data masking or redaction?
[00:06:51] Maya Lin: we offer payload redaction filters that can mask emails, ssns, or custom regex. for deeper PII protection we recommend client-side preprocessing or a proxy that strips PII before it reaches the API.
[00:07:03] Priya Shah: incident response and breach notification SLA?
[00:07:07] Jordan Reed: our incident response policy includes 24/7 on-call, and we commit to notify customers within 72 hours of a confirmed data breach; SLA specifics can be included in enterprise contract addendum.
[00:07:18] Priya Shah: curious about auditability of model outputs — we need to be able to correlate a generated output to the exact model hash and input for forensics.
[00:07:26] Maya Lin: we record model version, internal model hash/id, and request id for each response. you can attach your correlation id as part of the request, and that surfaces through logs and traces. for dedicated/private we can support longer retention of those artefacts for compliance investigations.
[00:07:44] Mark Delaney: performance and fallback — if you route to a cheaper model variant in a fallback, does payload leave EU?
[00:07:52] Jordan Reed: fallback policies can be constrained by region; you can set a policy that disallows cross-region fallback. we'll share policy examples.
[00:07:59] Priya Shah: how do you handle subpoenas / legal holds for data?
[00:08:05] Maya Lin: subpoenas are handled via our legal process; we notify customers unless prohibited by law, and we will surface the process in the contract. dedicated/private reduces Redwood's access surface which customers often prefer for legal containment.
[00:08:19] Elena Ortiz: curious, for the private on-prem option, what is the ops overhead — we are a small infra team.
[00:08:26] Jordan Reed: on-prem is heavier — you manage hardware, networking, and key custody. Redwood provides deployment automation, runbooks, and paid managed services if you want us to run it for you. dedicated (hosted in customer-dedicated tenancy) is often a good middle ground.
[00:08:42] Mark Delaney: do you support HSM integration like CloudHSM or Azure Dedicated HSM?
[00:08:47] Maya Lin: yes we integrate with CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM, and external HSMs via PKCS#11 in private deployments. for dedicated we can configure HSM-backed key operations in your tenancy.
[00:08:58] Priya Shah: SLA and audit logs retention — if we need 7 years retention for certain legal reasons, can you accommodate?
[00:09:06] Maya Lin: 7 years is atypical but possible in private/on-prem with your own storage. for hosted/dedicated, we offer extended retention add-ons and archived exports to your storage buckets. we'll need to scope storage costs in the quote.
[00:09:19] Jordan Reed: quick note — pricing impact for long retention and BYOK/HSM will be included in the dedicated/private proposal.
[00:09:26] Priya Shah: threat model — are you able to share the last three CVEs or high-level vulnerability history?
[00:09:33] Maya Lin: we can share anonymized CVE response summaries and the mitigation timeline; full details are in the pen test summary behind NDA.
[00:09:42] Elena Ortiz: logging fidelity — do logs capture full request payloads or truncated?
[00:09:47] Maya Lin: logs by default capture metadata and truncated payloads up to a configurable length; full payload capture is opt-in and we recommend redaction for pii.
[00:09:58] Mark Delaney: if we run an evaluation, we want to validate end-to-end that keys never leave our HSM. possible?
[00:10:05] Maya Lin: for a proper BYOK HSM-backed proof, dedicated or private will allow you to maintain master keys inside your HSM and only hand our runtime wrapped data keys; we can coordinate a test with your security team and run a short cryptographic proof-of-possession flow.
[00:10:22] Jordan Reed: ok, want to pivot to timeline and decision criteria — priya, what's your procurement time horizon?
[00:10:29] Priya Shah: we're aiming for a vendor selection by end of Q3, pilot in Q4, production early Q1 next year. must-haves: SOC2, BYOK/HSM option, EU data residency, SCIM/SSO integration, and audit log retention controls.
[00:10:45] Jordan Reed: noted. maya, do we have any reference architecture that maps to their must-haves?
[00:10:50] Maya Lin: yes i'll pull private control plane + HSM integration and a dedicated reserved capacity architecture that keeps data in EU regions.
[00:10:58] Priya Shah: one more — can redwood support encryption of in-transit telemetry too? we have FIPS requirements around TLS ciphers.
[00:11:06] Maya Lin: we support TLS 1.2+ with configurable cipher suites in private/dedicated; hosted has our standard TLS configuration which meets industry requirements, but for FIPS-specific cipher lists we'd recommend dedicated/private.
[00:11:18] Elena Ortiz: do you provide artifact retention proof for audits — like immutable logs?
[00:11:23] Maya Lin: we provide append-only audit logs and can integrate with WORM storage in your cloud bucket for immutability. we'll include doc references in the packet.
[00:11:33] Jordan Reed: great. any blockers on proceeding with NDA so we can share SOC2 and pen test artifacts?
[00:11:39] Priya Shah: we'll review the NDA but yes that would be helpful.
[00:11:42] Jordan Reed: quick recap: we will share SOC2 & pen test, BYOK docs, private deployment checklist, and schedule a technical deep dive between maya and mark. action items in an email after this call.
[00:11:55] Mark Delaney: sounds good.
[00:11:58] Priya Shah: do you have a sample contract clause for data residency and egress restrictions?
[00:12:04] Jordan Reed: yes we'll include a sample residency clause and the SLA paragraph for regional routing and fallback.
[00:12:10] Elena Ortiz: timeline-wise we'll aim to return NDA and artifact list by EOD Monday.
[00:12:16] Jordan Reed: perfect. thanks everyone. maya anything to add?
[00:12:20] Maya Lin: i'll follow up with a network diagram template and a checklist for HSM integration steps.
[00:12:26] Jordan Reed: thanks — we'll close there.

Notes: conversation had some cross-talk and short interruptions; transcription may have occasional misheard acronyms ("sample" for SAML, "soc two" spelled phonetically). Full artifacts to be shared via secured link pending NDA.
